subject: Re: Prompt collection & model-fit follow-up — Acme discovery
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme-corp.com>, Priya Menon <priya.m@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Prompt collection & model-fit follow-up — Acme discovery

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion on where Acme wants to embed the assistant (support articles + approval workflow) and the biggest failure modes (PII in freeform notes, short legal snippets, and multi-turn context across edits). As promised, a short recap and clear next steps so we can start model-fit evaluation: 

1) Recommended starting models: redwood-large-v1 for baseline quality, and redwood-quant-l6 for a lower-cost, quantized option. We’ll run both on your prompt set and report token costs + latency tradeoffs.

2) Benchmarks I’ll run: accuracy on intent classification (your severity labels), generation quality on 200 random prompts, hallucination regression vs your previous system, and redaction safety checks. I’ll link the initial benchmark template below.

3) Action for Acme: please send 100–300 representative prompts (CSV) including:
   - normal/common prompts
   - edge cases (truncated sentences, legal boilerplate, and mixed English/Spanish)
   - any prompts that contain PII you would expect redaction for (we’ll redact in our env, but need to test detection)

4) Redaction guidance: if possible, tag any prompt rows that should be considered PII-sensitive in your CSV (column: pii_flag). If you can’t tag, we’ll treat all freeform notes as candidate PII and run our automated redaction checks — but explicit tagging speeds things up.

5) Timeline: if you can share prompts by Mon 29 Jun EOD PT, we’ll return an initial model-fit report and benchmark PDF by Thu 2 Jul.

Attachments: I’m attaching our benchmark template (redwood_benchmarks_202606.pdf) and example CSV header we prefer.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Rishi (in cc) for the technical evaluation and Dylan for prompt-format guidance once we have the file.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.m@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt collection & model-fit follow-up — Acme discovery

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary. Attaching our initial prompt export (acme_prompt_samples.csv). A couple notes:

- We included 140 rows, with a rough "pii_flag" column where available. Some legacy rows don't have the flag.
- We have a handful of edge cases: two mixed-language prompts (EN/ES), several legal clause snippets, and some truncated customer notes coming from mobile.
- Curious about redaction: do you run redaction before or after passing to the model? We need to understand what we can control on our side.

Also, is redwood-quant-l6 expected to degrade on legal snippet fidelity? That’s an area we care about.

Attaching: acme_prompt_samples.csv

Thanks,
Alex
Director, AI Integrations
Acme Corp
alex.j@acme-corp.com

To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt collection & model-fit follow-up — Acme discovery

Alex —

Got the CSV, thanks — I downloaded acme_prompt_samples.csv and started a quick pass. A few clarifications and proposed next steps: 

- Redaction flow: we recommend redaction before inference for PII removal. Redwood can run a deterministic redaction pass (PII detector -> token-level masking) in your private eval environment and provide both the redacted prompt + a report of what was removed. We do keep an option to run a model-based post-filter for additional safety checks, but for your use-case (legal snippets) pre-inference redaction reduces risk of leakage.

- Model fidelity: redwood-quant-l6 will likely show small regressions on very dense legal language. That said, our benchmarks often show parity for short-span factual extraction tasks; long legal clause generation is where the full-size model holds an edge. We’ll quantify this for your edge cases.

- Request: can you add a short set of expected outputs for ~30 of the prompts (just one or two lines each) so we can score quality automatically? If you can’t, we’ll run human review for a smaller sample.

- Next call: propose a 30-minute technical sync on Wed 30 Jun at 10am PT — Rishi (cc) will lead the model-fit discussion. Is that time okay?

We’ll run both models on the set you sent and return an initial benchmark PDF and a ZIP with redacted prompts and scoring artifacts.

Best,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme prompt set & model-fit ask (for follow-up)

Marissa / Dylan —

Thanks for the heads-up and for sharing the CSV. I started a quick scan of the sample file in the shared drive link you posted. Notes for our run:

- We should run both redwood-large-v1 and redwood-quant-l6, plus a constrained decoding pass for legal-clause prompts to reduce hallucinations.
- For scoring: create an automated EM/ROUGE-like pass for the 30 seeded expected outputs Alex will provide, and plan ~20 human eval checks for multi-turn context cases.
- Redaction: confirm we run deterministic pre-inference PII masking; Dylan to prepare an anonymized sample output showing redaction artifacts.

I’ll prepare the benchmark runbook and upload results to the linked folder. Marissa — can you confirm the Wed 30 Jun 10am PT slot for the technical sync? I’ll invite the infra group if we need GPU profiling.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
